text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Large Swedish companies made billions of crowns on speculation about the crown when it fell sharply in 1992, but taxpayers lost money when the currency's value decreased.
- Sweden had the lowest inflation in the European Union in September, with prices rising by 0.2 percent for the month.

- Swedish companies are well represented in Shanghai, with offices for ABB, Atlas Copco, Electrolux and Ericsson already doing business in China. Prime Minister Goran Persson is planning a visit to Shanghai later this month.

- Centre Party leader Olof Johansson calls for the resignation of Riksbank governing board chairman Kjell-Olof Feldt because of his positive attitude towards a Swedish link to the European Union's monetary union.
However, an independent central bank is a requirement for membership in the European Union's monetary union.
- A Stockholm parking company has proposed an underground parking lot under the Stockholm island of Djurgarden, site of luxury properties and parks.

- Prime Minister Goran Persson says during an official visit to Moscow in a Russian television interview that Sweden can act as a mediator in talks about NATO expansion because of its non-aligned status.
- Scandinavian Airlines System SAS hopes to launch two weekly flights to Shanghai and has a good chance of sucessfully negotiating this for a 1997 start, newspaper sources say.

- Sweden's largest commecial television channel TV4, which posted a loss of 40 million crowns in the first nine months of 1996, aims to increase sponsored broadcasts and children's programmes in order to swing back to profit.
